public_comment.topic: Argues the override failed due to lost public confidence, not messaging; cites accreditation risk and reading proficiency, urges review of support programs, academic prioritization, IEP audit, and accountability.

public_comment.speaker_as_heard: Matt Nzareno (heard also as Matt Ezaro)
public_comment.topic: Presented a by-sport athletics cost/revenue analysis built from FY24 actuals, arguing middle school sports were revenue-positive and questioning the decision to cut them for budget reasons.
Spoke on behalf of the community about restoring middle school athletics, requesting a detailed cost/revenue breakdown by sport and guidance on applying community-raised funds, by mid-July.

Requested permission to purchase five football helmets and to fund one-way transportation to away games using booster funds, and pushed back on the characterization of football boosters as "wealthier" than other programs.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 389 Mus[?] Road, speaking for the music boosters ("musicators")
public_comment.topic: Raised the fundraising policy's two-fundraiser limit, asked for guidance on donating funds for color guard/marching band uniforms and transportation, requested restoring fifth grade band and sixth grade jazz, and raised concerns about scheduling forcing students to choose between electives and academics.

budget_items.what_was_said: A donation from an author visit event at Turkey Hill Elementary was presented for deposit into the elementary gift account.
Funds were moved from the salary reserve account to about 13 salary lines in deficit (mostly substitutes), partly due to a departing employee's vacation payout.

budget_items.what_was_said: Unspent athletic transportation budget was transferred to cover an overage in athletic dues and fees (association/game fees).

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer - equipment reconditioning to new equipment
budget_items.what_was_said: Funds were moved from equipment reconditioning to cover a new equipment overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer - grant-funded salary to extended day
budget_items.what_was_said: A portion of a staff member's grant-funded salary was moved to the extended day line; a transposition error in the amount was caught and corrected on the sheet.
Warrants for the period were presented for signature; no vote was required.
The district secured an additional state earmark for FY27 facilities improvements, with projects still being finalized including ADA door access, HVAC controls, generator work, and gym lighting.
A public commenter said middle school athletics were eliminated as a budget reduction following the failed override, out of a much larger overall budget.

budget_items.topic: Middle school sports revenue (public comment analysis)
budget_items.what_was_said: A parent's analysis claimed middle school sports were revenue-positive, effectively offsetting a football deficit, based on FY24 actuals and an assumed athletic fee.
A parent cited field hockey officiating cost as an example of low direct operating cost per official.
A parent estimated the cost of the golf program to give the committee a directional range rather than an exact figure.
The football boosters president asked permission to purchase helmets and to fund one-way transportation to away games using booster funds.
Supplies were reported as almost fully expended for the year, cited as evidence of close budget management by the superintendent and business manager.
The available salary budget balance was reported, to be combined with the salary reserve for a full picture.

budget_items.topic: FY26 estimated year-end return to town
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager gave a running estimate of funds likely to be returned to the town at year end, including a newly added custodial payroll figure, noting the estimate is still being refined downward.
A member praised last year's surplus as evidence of a change in fiscal management, noting the current estimated return is in line with prior years and other departments.
The chair described additional state cherry sheet funding coming to Lunenburg beyond what the town budget assumed, citing differences between the Senate, House and Governor's budget figures.

The town is receiving additional one-time snow and ice removal money, distinguished from the recurring chapter 70 ask; the school department is typically allowed to run a deficit on snow/ice, covered by free cash.

The chair read total estimated state receipts and estimated charges (assessments) figures from the cherry sheet, noting the charges side includes items like MBTA assessment (described as having doubled) and charter/school choice tuition.

budget_items.topic: Charter school and school choice tuition
budget_items.what_was_said: The district spends roughly equal amounts on charter school and school choice tuition for students leaving the district, with the school choice figure expected to increase.

budget_items.topic: Placeholder ask for special town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: A member proposed using a placeholder estimate for the special town meeting ask, pending the final state budget figure, to be spent mainly on literacy professional development and Ignite tutoring.
The chair stated that chapter 70 funding covers a large share of the entire Lunenburg school budget.
The high-dosage tutoring program was funded through a supplemental state budget grant; members are uncertain it will be available again.
The superintendent said Lunenburg spends well above its state-calculated foundation budget yet remains near the bottom of the list for per-pupil spending compared to peer districts.
A booster asked whether a small amount of funding could restore the cut fifth grade band program, citing its low cost.

decisions.decision: Grades 3 and 4 will no longer be departmentalized next year; students will have one teacher rather than rotating teams, based on research on relationship-building at that age.
There will be zero reading interventionist positions at Turkey Hill and zero at the Primary school next year, described as a necessary cut.
A guidance document on booster club donations and Title IX compliance protocols has been finalized and shared with booster organizations.
Discussion of specific booster funding requests (helmets, transportation) for football and other sports will be taken up as agenda items at the July 29th meeting.
Going into next year's budget process, all extracurricular activities and athletics are considered "on the table" for further reductions.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee heard extensive public comment on middle school athletics funding, booster fundraising, and academic performance following the failed override, then reviewed routine business (minutes, a donation, four line-item transfers, warrants, and encumbrances). The superintendent reported on transportation vans, a facilities earmark, staffing changes, and Title IX/booster-donation guidance; the committee also approved an adult meal price increase, relocated the T-ball program to accommodate the food pantry, accepted a curriculum report describing the loss of all reading interventionists and larger class sizes, accepted a strong FY26 quarterly budget report, accepted a personnel report with numerous departures attributed to budget uncertainty, and voted unanimously to ask the select board to convene a special town meeting to direct additional state chapter 70 and other cherry sheet funds into the school budget.
minutes.headline: The committee voted unanimously to ask the select board for a special town meeting to redirect state aid into the school budget.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every vote outcome that both actually record, on the headline dollar figures that appear in both (warrants once corrected, the $175,000 facilities earmark, the $14,415/$29M athletics cut, the $19,400 middle-school revenue figure, the $350 fee, the $50 officiating cost, the $1,500 transportation ask, and the 35% Chapter 70 share), and on the major decisions (Title IX/booster guidance, deferring specific booster requests to July 29, "everything on the table" for FY28 athletics). The most consequential gaps are: the official minutes never itemize the four transfer amounts or most of the superintendent's/business manager's dollar figures (chapter 70 add, state aid, tuition, Ignite grant, foundation-budget %) that our minutes captured from the recording; our minutes omit Vice Chair Anthony Sculimbrene entirely despite his making most of the meeting's motions; and two votes (curriculum report, personnel report) show a discrepancy in outcome detail — "not audible" vs. a recorded unanimous approval, and a noted abstention vs. "all approve" — that should be checked against the recording.
